purpose: Revision 6 changes on top of the v1/v4/v5 tables (earlier configs stay unchanged so v1-v5 rebuild byte-identically): Korean software keyboard (font group, labels, input hints), Korean manual pictures, error heading size.
keyboard_font_reason: The keyboard loads only glyph group 'wii_name' of /cnt/00000008/wbf1.brfna (executable 0x80054dc4-0x80054e0c: SCGetProductArea != JPN -> 'wii_name' at 0x8088ddd8, JPN -> every group). In the Korean 43K wbf1 'wii_name' = sheets 38 and 49-55; KS X 1001 Hangul ('ksx_level_1') = sheets 38-48, so v2 drew '?'. v6 flags sheets 39-48 for 'wii_name' in the GLGR block (no other byte changes).
keyboard_rows_keep_english_reason: Key caps stay as printed on Korean keyboards (Space, like Shift/Caps in the layout and lng entries 545/561); command buttons use the v1 Korean rows (OK, Quit, Dictionary, Close, More, Back).
keyboard_labels_reason: Two UTF-16 copies of the prediction-dictionary language abbreviations (each 8-byte slot, followed by the EU codes EN/DE/FR/ES/IT/NL which stay). A three-syllable label plus terminator fills the slot exactly.
lng_hints_reason: v4 kept these keyboard input hints English because the keyboard font could not draw Hangul; v6 uses their v1 Korean translations.
error_heading_reason: Opera breaks Hangul between any two syllables; at 130% the most common heading '240023: 서버를 찾을 수 없습니다.' wrapped as '없습니/다.' (lead review of v5). About 15% smaller heading text keeps it on one line [추정: measured from the v5 wrap point].
